title: Choose Consumit's redesign direction
question: The roll assigned Screening Arcade. Keep it, choose an alternate, or reroll. Every option keeps Consumit's original orange brand; your choice will guide the redesign of every screen and shared component.

options.label: Screening Arcade
options.lineage: Late-night arcade cabinets, cinema marquees, and the fun of choosing what to play next.
options.thesis: Make choosing a story feel playful, then make Play the quickest move.
options.viewport: Home opens with a small, useful night picker beside one fully legible featured title; orange Play, format paths, and a quiet Circle doorway remain easy to find.
options.risk: Arcade cues can turn a useful film journal into a game interface.

raised.raise: One controlled focal area makes every screen easy to scan.
Diary and review activity can unfold in a clear, sequential reading rhythm.
A single overlapping poster layer supplies depth without adding routine shadows.
Selection and playback states stay discrete, named, and unmistakable.
Universal search stays keyboard-first and visible.
Motion is limited to one short, optional transition; content remains still and available.

options.label: Pocket Film Zine
options.lineage: Independent film fanzines and the little ticket stubs tucked inside them.
options.thesis: Give every screening the personality of a page worth keeping and passing around.
options.viewport: Home reads like a new issue: a clear cover story leads into short discovery columns, member writing, and a visible Play action.
options.risk: Editorial detail may slow down members who want to start watching quickly.

options.label: Movie Panels
options.lineage: Silver-age comic pages: panels, Ben-Day dots, and expressive captions.
options.thesis: Let discovery and diary entries read as small stories instead of rows of media.
options.viewport: One title owns the opening panel; smaller panels lead to formats, Circle activity, and fast follow-up choices.
options.case: Strong audience energy and a clear sequence; its expressive panels compete with the direct Play path.
options.risk: Speech bubbles and bursts can make reviews and controls noisy.

options.label: House Lights
options.lineage: A theatre lighting desk, with named cues and a single lit stage.
options.thesis: Use light and darkness to guide the eye from a title choice into its screening.
options.viewport: A quiet dark stage frames one title and its Play decision, with smaller cues for friends and the next programme.
options.case: Strong cinema identity and focal control; it offers less playful exploration than the requested experience.
options.risk: The theatre metaphor can repeat a standard streaming hero.

options.label: Layered Papercut
options.lineage: Symmetrical folk papercuts made from flat pieces of colored paper.
options.case: Fuses weakly with fast streaming and social tasks; keeping one clear overlapping layer adds useful depth.
options.kept: Use one measured overlap to separate artwork from controls without adding shadow stacks.

options.label: Game Boy Field
options.lineage: A four-shade handheld game screen with tile-based navigation.
options.case: The pixel limit makes real artwork, title copy, and dense diary rows harder to scan; keep its explicit selection states.
options.kept: Selection and playback states have one discrete, named visual treatment.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.lineage: A green-phosphor text terminal in a dark machine room.
options.case: A terminal is a poor model for poster-led choice and expressive member profiles; preserve its efficient keyboard path.
options.kept: Search and navigation remain fast from the keyboard with visible focus.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.lineage: A full-screen GPU shader with cursor-reactive distortion and scene transitions.
options.case: Ambient rendering adds cost and distraction without helping members pick, play, or remember a title.
options.kept: Use only a short, reduced-motion-aware transition when a selection changes.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar catalogue with a strong featured title and polished poster rails.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional responsive entertainment homepage with clear Movies, Series, Anime, Library, and Play destinations.
canonCard.risk: It is easy to understand but could resemble every other streaming service.
